text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى ٱلْحَوَارِيِّۦنَ أَنْ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِى وَبِرَسُولِى قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَٱشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنَا مُسْلِمُونَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the next recalled favor scene
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as continuation. With the following temporal marker, it carries the reader into another recalled favor scene in the Jesus discourse rather than a detached new report. Its light onset also keeps the opening heard as a compact paired launch, not as a separated pause before the recall frame.

topics.headline: opening connector continues the recalled-favor chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens as the next remembered favor in the Jesus discourse, not as a detached report.
topics.reason: The opening conjunction coheres with the temporal frame and the surrounding recalled-scene sequence in 5:110-115.

words.gloss_range: past-time recall marker that turns the event into a remembered scene
words.prose: {{ar:إِذْ}} ({{tr:idh}}) frames the event as remembered time. The inspiration to the disciples is therefore heard as “recall when” within the continuing sequence of scenes in 5:110-115.

topics.headline: past-time marker functions as recall trigger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the inspiration event is being summoned into memory as part of a chain of scenes, not issued as a present command.
topics.reason: The temporal adverb is strongly licensed as the frame for the inspiration scene and matches the repeated recall pattern across 5:110-115.

words.gloss_range: completed first-person divine inspiration, objectless until its content is opened by the following clause
words.root_gloss_range: swift, subtle, information-bearing communication; locally a completed divine act whose content is supplied by the following content clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْحَيْتُ}} ({{tr:awḥaytu}}) first establishes a completed divine act: God’s first-person agency is built into the verb, while the message itself waits for the following content clause. The root’s hidden, swift communication range makes the act feel like subtle information-bearing inspiration, and here that communication reaches the disciples as non-prophet recipients before becoming a command to believe in God and His messenger.

topics.headline: completed first-person act before content is disclosed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the act of divine inspiration first, with God’s first-person agency embedded in the verb before the command content appears.
topics.reason: The perfect first-person form and objectless local valence are supported by QAC and attachment evidence; the following content clause supplies the message.

topics.headline: subtle communication moves toward non-prophet recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hidden, information-bearing inspiration is directed to the disciples themselves, extending divine communication into the inner circle.
topics.reason: The local prepositional recipient and root evidence support swift concealed communication while keeping the local event distinct from public proclamation.

topics.headline: inspiration produces belief in the sent messenger
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine communication immediately takes the shape of belief in God and His messenger, not a private feeling without doctrinal content.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence rows are locally anchored by the following command and messenger complement.

topics.headline: minor acoustic texture without separate payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The acoustic note does not add a distinct reader-facing payoff beyond the retained concealed-communication topic.
topics.reason: The acoustic note does not add a distinct reader-facing payoff beyond the retained concealed-communication topic.

words.gloss_range: directional recipient marker for inspiration, toward rather than directly objectifying the disciples
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَى}} ({{tr:ilā}}) routes the inspiration toward its endpoint. The preposition makes the disciples recipients of directed communication and fits a recurring directed-inspiration formula (4:163, 14:13); the non-imposition contrast is useful only as a nuance of direction, not as a separate local doctrine.

topics.headline: toward-recipient path for inspiration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the inspiration is grammatically routed toward a selected recipient group before the command content is named.
topics.reason: The preposition clearly marks direction and recipient endpoint; the contrast with an imposition frame is preserved only as a local directional nuance, not as a broad theology of coercion.

words.gloss_range: definite human plural disciple-title, governed as the recipient group and later resumed as speakers and believers
words.root_gloss_range: purity, refinement, return, and dialogue-adjacent associations; locally narrowed to the Jesus-specific disciple title with purified inner-circle pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحَوَارِيِّۦنَ}} ({{tr:al-ḥawāriyyīna}}) names the known disciple circle as the recipient of the inspiration and the later source of the reply. The title carries purified-companion pressure, return to aligned response, and dialogue-colored speech potential from its root family, but local usage narrows these pressures to the Jesus-specific disciple group seen in 3:52 and 61:14, now placed inside divine recall and carried forward to 5:112.

topics.headline: known human disciple group anchors later response
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the disciples first as a definite inner-circle recipient group that later becomes the speaking collective.
topics.reason: The noun is governed as recipient of the inspiration and supplies the referent for later plural speech and belief forms.

topics.headline: purity-root pressure inside a specialized title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the title is not a generic follower word; it carries refined companion pressure while local usage keeps it as the Jesus-specific disciple title.
topics.reason: Root-family pressures of purification, return, and dialogue are preserved as title coloration, but the local form and distribution narrow the sense to the recognized disciples.

topics.headline: disciple formula continues across Jesus passages
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group belongs to a repeated disciple formula seen in 3:52 and 61:14, while 5:111 relocates the response inside divine inspiration.
topics.reason: The intertextual rows give concrete parallels and the adjacent 5:112 recurrence, so the formulaic disciple role survives as a local payoff.

topics.headline: paradisal comparison overextends the local title
topics.blocking_evidence: The local word is the Jesus-specific disciple title; shared root evidence alone does not make the paradisal beings in 44:54, 52:20, or 56:22 part of the local sense.
topics.reason: The shared root does not license importing the paradisal beings of 44:54, 52:20, and 56:22 into this local disciple title.

topics.headline: sound texture without independent payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The sound observation is decorative once the title, recipient role, and formulaic distribution have been retained.
topics.reason: The sound observation is decorative once the title, recipient role, and formulaic distribution have been retained.

words.gloss_range: content-opening particle that makes the inspiration disclose itself as a command
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) is the doorway from hidden inspiration into stated content. Because it opens onto an imperative, the particle lets the reader hear the communication as “namely, believe” or as commanded content without losing the hinge function.

topics.headline: particle opens inspiration as command content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact hinge where hidden inspiration becomes an explicit command to believe.
topics.reason: The particle is syntactically forced as the content complement; explanatory and infinitival analyses both support its doorway function without requiring a single overexclusive label.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative command to believe or place trust, governed through following bāʾ complements rather than a direct object
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, faith, confirmation, and entrusting; locally selected as a plural imperative to enter trusting belief
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامِنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āminū}}) is the core command inside the inspiration. Its root carries trust and security pressure, while the plural imperative and following bāʾ complements select the local sense of entering belief in God and His messenger; the same root will return as the disciples’ completed reply. The command also sits in a belief-messenger and belief-witness network, with same-surah pressure from 5:12 and 5:83.

topics.headline: imperative makes inspiration directive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the content of inspiration is not information about belief but a plural command that is later answered by the same root.
topics.reason: The imperative form, plural address, and later perfect response make the command-response structure local and explicit.

topics.headline: belief enters trust through governed complements
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief is not a bare abstraction; it is entered and then attached through the following complements to God and His messenger.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows prepositional complements rather than a direct object, so the objectless command and the following bāʾ phrases must be read together.

topics.headline: faith command carries security and entrusted-commitment pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command asks for settled trust and security-bearing commitment, while local grammar selects the imperative belief sense.
topics.reason: The root field supports security and entrusting pressure, but the local Form IV imperative and bāʾ complements keep belief or trusting commitment as the selected sense.

topics.headline: belief command joins messenger and witness networks
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this command sits in a wider belief-messenger and belief-witness pattern, with local echoes to 5:12, 5:83, and the later reply in 5:111.
topics.reason: The intertextual and co-occurrence rows are concretely anchored by the messenger complement and the later witness request.

words.gloss_range: fused preposition and divine first-person pronoun marking God as the first object and ground of trust
words.prose: {{ar:بِى}} ({{tr:bī}}) fuses the preposition to the divine first-person pronoun. The speaker of the inspiration becomes the first object and ground of the commanded trust before the messenger is added.

topics.headline: first-person divine object leads the belief pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the divine speaker becoming the first object and ground of the trust He commands before the messenger is named.
topics.reason: The fused preposition-pronoun is governed by the command and its order before the messenger complement is locally explicit.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction pairing the two belief complements without collapsing them
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the two belief complements without merging them. The command requires trust in God and in His messenger as a coordinated pair, while the repeated bāʾ keeps the attachments distinct.

topics.headline: conjunction joins without merging belief objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief in God and belief in His messenger are coordinated as one command while remaining grammatically distinct attachments.
topics.reason: The conjunction and repeated bāʾ produce a parallel pair without collapsing the two complements into one object.

words.gloss_range: repeated bāʾ that gives the messenger his own governed belief-complement
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) repeats the governing marker for the messenger. That repetition gives the second complement its own attachment under the same belief command instead of letting it trail as a loose addition.

topics.headline: second bāʾ gives messenger distinct governance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the messenger is not loosely appended; the repeated bāʾ places him under the same belief command as a distinct governed complement.
topics.reason: The second preposition is syntactically forced before the messenger and preserves balanced but ordered coordination.

words.gloss_range: singular possessed messenger, the second governed object of commanded belief
words.root_gloss_range: sending, dispatch, message-bearing, and delegated mission; locally the possessed singular messenger whose authority derives from the divine sender
words.prose: {{ar:رَسُولِى}} ({{tr:rasūlī}}) is the possessed singular messenger: the envoy’s authority is tied to the divine speaker by the suffix and by the sending-root. The word therefore makes belief in the messenger derivative of God’s sending, not a competing object beside God. Because the complement is separately governed, the belief-in-messenger formula remains distinct while preparing the witness field that follows.

topics.headline: possessive singular localizes messenger authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the messenger as God’s own singular envoy in this scene, not as an independent or generic authority.
topics.reason: The genitive governance, construct definiteness, and first-person suffix all tie the messenger to the divine speaker.

topics.headline: sent-agent image supports mediated belief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief in the messenger means trusting the sent channel and delegated mission, while local grammar keeps the word as the possessed envoy.
topics.reason: The root field of sending and message-bearing is locally relevant because the noun is a messenger under divine possession and under the belief command.

topics.headline: messenger belief stays distinct within wider formulas
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the messenger complement as part of a repeated belief-in-messenger demand that also prepares the ayah’s witness language.
topics.reason: The repeated-governance formula and the surah-local messenger field support this as a meaningful downstream topic.

topics.headline: minor sound image without separate payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The acoustic image does not add a separate reader-facing payoff beyond the retained sending and messenger topics.
topics.reason: The acoustic image does not add a separate reader-facing payoff beyond the retained sending and messenger topics.

words.gloss_range: third-person plural perfect speech verb shifting from divine narration to the disciples’ voiced response
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speech, declaration, and externalized utterance; locally a completed collective response introducing direct speech
words.prose: {{ar:قَالُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:qālū}}) pivots the ayah from divine narration into the disciples’ spoken response. Hidden inspiration becomes audible declaration, and the basic speech verb opens the direct discourse that runs to the ayah’s end. It also places this answer inside a nearby Jesus-discourse speech chain (5:109, 5:110, 5:112, 5:113), where saying can mark denial, testimony, acceptance, or further dialogue.

topics.headline: speech verb pivots from divine command to disciple reply
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse changing hands: divine narration gives way to the disciples’ completed collective speech.
topics.reason: The verb introduces the quoted response and resolves its omitted subject back to the disciples.

topics.headline: internal reception becomes spoken declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that concealed inspiration is externalized as plain speech whose content is belief and request for testimony.
topics.reason: The basic speech verb and its following quoted content support the move from internal reception to audible declaration.

topics.headline: saying root participates in nearby dialogue chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the response as one speech event in a nearby chain of Jesus-discourse sayings, not as an isolated quotation.
topics.reason: The concrete nearby references in the row make the local speech-chain payoff usable.

topics.headline: minor acoustic break without separate payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The sound note is decorative after the discourse-pivot and speech-externalization topics are preserved.
topics.reason: The sound note is decorative after the discourse-pivot and speech-externalization topics are preserved.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural perfect declaration of accomplished belief, compactly covering the prior belief objects
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, faith, confirmation, and settled commitment; locally a completed collective declaration answering the command
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنَّا}} ({{tr:āmannā}}) answers the command with a completed collective declaration. It leaves the objects unstated because the prior command supplied them, and the root’s trust-security pressure makes the reply sound like settled commitment moving toward witness and submission.

topics.headline: completed belief answers the imperative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the disciples turning the command to believe into an already-accomplished collective declaration.
topics.reason: The perfect first-person plural form mirrors the earlier imperative root while changing person and mood into compliance.

topics.headline: compact belief reply inherits earlier objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply does not need to restate God and messenger because the preceding command already supplied the belief objects.
topics.reason: The objectless perfect is locally recoverable from the prior bāʾ-governed command; the 3:52 contrast clarifies the omission without overriding this ayah.

topics.headline: belief becomes settled speech moving toward submission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices belief as a voiced, settled trust that becomes the first half of a larger move toward witness and submitted identity.
topics.reason: Root pressure, speech framing, and the following witness request all support the belief-to-testimony-to-submission sequence.

words.gloss_range: conjunction holding the declaration open for a coordinated witness-request
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the response from closing after “we have believed.” It coordinates the belief declaration with a second speech act, the request that the disciples’ state be witnessed.

topics.headline: conjunction keeps declaration open for witness request
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the disciples’ answer does not stop at “we have believed”; the conjunction carries it into a request for attestation.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates two distinct speech acts inside the quoted response and prevents the declaration from closing the reply.

words.gloss_range: singular imperative to bear witness, with its content supplied by a bāʾ plus clause construction
words.root_gloss_range: witnessing as presence, observation, clarification, and testimony; locally a direct singular imperative request for attestation
words.prose: {{ar:ٱشْهَدْ}} ({{tr:ishhad}}) reverses the command direction: those commanded to believe now ask a singular addressee to bear witness. The addressee remains grammatically open, but the witness root keeps presence, observation, clarification, and attestation together after the contested clarity and magic field of 5:110, and the following bāʾ-clause makes the object of testimony a whole proposition; the same belief-and-witness pattern is visible in 3:52 and carried forward locally in 5:113.

topics.headline: disciples answer command with singular witness request
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a reversal in speech force: the commanded disciples now ask one addressee to bear witness, while the morphology leaves that addressee contextually open.
topics.reason: The second-masculine singular imperative is clear, but the addressee remains ambiguous between Jesus and God within the discourse frame.

topics.headline: witnessing combines presence and declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request seeks more than approval; it asks for present attestation of the disciples’ submitted state.
topics.reason: The root field supports presence, observation, clarification, and testimony, while Form I directly commands the witness act.

topics.headline: testimony content comes through a bāʾ-clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is witnessed is a whole proposition, not a simple noun object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows the content introduced through the following bāʾ plus complementizer construction rather than a direct object.

topics.headline: belief and witness formula echoes across scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the witness request belongs to a repeated belief-and-witness formula, especially the disciple formula in 3:52 and the local witness continuation in 5:113.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete formula and same-surah links, so the intertext survives without controlling the local parse.

topics.headline: minor crisp sound texture without separate payoff
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The phonetic note adds no distinct payoff after the imperative, witness-root, constructional, and formula topics are retained.
topics.reason: The phonetic note adds no distinct payoff after the imperative, witness-root, constructional, and formula topics are retained.

words.gloss_range: preposition attaching the witness request to the proposition being attested
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches the witness request to its content. It points to the fact to be attested, not to an accusation against the disciples, and it opens the final testimony-content unit. In 5:111 it binds to the expanded following complementizer, a local surface difference from the shorter witness formula in 3:52.

topics.headline: bāʾ attaches witness to a proposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the preposition turning the witness request toward “that we are submitters” as an attested proposition, not an accusation against the disciples.
topics.reason: The bāʾ-clause is syntactically forced as testimony content; the 3:52 form comparison is useful as a variant-like contrast but does not replace this local form.

words.gloss_range: emphatic complementizer with plural pronoun introducing the witnessed identity-clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّنَا}} ({{tr:annanā}}) brings the witnessed proposition into emphatic form. The expanded complementizer keeps the collective “we” visible before the final predicate names what the group is.

topics.headline: expanded complementizer carries the witnessed “we”
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the proposition becoming emphatic and collective before the final predicate names the disciples’ identity.
topics.reason: The complementizer plus plural pronoun introduces a nominal predication and keeps the group subject visible inside the witnessed content.

words.gloss_range: masculine plural active participial predicate closing the ayah with the disciples’ standing identity
words.root_gloss_range: submission, surrender, safety, peace, and soundness; locally an active participle naming an enduring submitted identity
words.prose: {{ar:مُسْلِمُونَ}} ({{tr:muslimūna}}) closes the ayah as an active participial identity: the disciples are submitters as an ongoing state, not merely people who performed one act. The root’s safety, peace, and wholeness pressure makes the submitted identity feel like wholeness-through-yielding, while the structure makes submission the climax after command and belief; the same disciple formula appears in 3:52. The final long plural ending gives that identity a stable acoustic landing.

topics.headline: active participle makes submission a standing identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes on a durable group identity, not a one-time act of submitting.
topics.reason: The active participle functions as the predicate of the complementizer clause and agrees with the collective subject.

topics.headline: submission identity carries safety and wholeness pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that submitted identity is colored by safety, peace, and soundness, while local grammar keeps “submitters” as the selected predicate.
topics.reason: The root field supports peace and wholeness pressure, but the Form IV active participle and predicative slot keep the local sense anchored in submission.

topics.headline: belief command culminates in submitted identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ordered rise from command to belief to submitted identity, with the 3:52 disciple formula confirming that the term marks disposition rather than a later sectarian label.
topics.reason: The final position, belief pairing, and concrete parallels such as 3:52 support the climactic function.

topics.headline: long plural ending gives closure to the final identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final plural ending giving the submission identity a stable closing sound.
topics.reason: The acoustic closure is locally tied to the final word and its plural nominative identity, so it has a small but real payoff.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَوْحَيْتُ ... ءَامِنُوا۟ ... قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَٱشْهَدْ ... مُسْلِمُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: A concealed impartation prompts trust, the recipients externalize that trust as speech, and they place their yielded self-description under divine attestation.

activation_trace.role: Hidden delivery of knowledge supplies the inward starting point of the sequence.
Heart-settling assent links the commanded act to the disciples' repeated response.
Articulated speech moves the inward assent into an inspectable public reply.
Knowledgeable attestation makes God the addressee who can establish their claim.
Handing over or relinquishing an affair supplies the final posture named by the group.

changed_reading.before: A command to believe followed by a verbal profession.
changed_reading.after: A hidden divine communication travels through settled assent into public, witnessed self-yielding.

baseline_models.mechanism: The addressed helpers are not passive endpoints: the carried message reaches them, they answer it in speech, and their request for witness closes a reciprocal message-response loop.

activation_trace.role: The helper or supporter image gives the recipients a participatory social function.
Conversational return makes their spoken answer part of the helper role.
Messenger and carried message provide the relational channel to which the helpers respond.
Their utterance returns the received charge as an owned communal statement.
Invoked presence closes the loop by locating their response before a witness.

changed_reading.before: A group receives an instruction and agrees.
changed_reading.after: A helper community completes the message's circuit by returning it as its own witnessed response.

context_deltas.mechanism: Obedience to God and the messenger, the messenger's bounded work of delivery, and a test that reveals conduct toward what is unseen turn the focus profession from bare cognition into allegiance made legible in response.

activation_trace.role: The focus repeats reassuring assent as both command and answer.
The messenger image anchors the profession to a borne message rather than an abstract second object.
Obedient yielding supplies the behavioral form in which professed trust becomes visible.
Message-delivery bounds the messenger's function and clarifies the channel named in the focus.
A test that makes a state appear converts inward trust into an exposed disposition.
What is hidden from sight links tested conduct back to the focus's concealed communication.

structural_cues: Faith recurs across 5:87-94 amid commands, restraint, and repeated action.
5:92 pairs obedience to God and the messenger, then limits the messenger to clear conveyance.
The focus repeats ء م ن on both sides of the command-response boundary.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated faith, obedience, delivered message, and an unseen-revealing test; I infer that the focus reply claims enacted allegiance, while the live alternative is simple verbal assent without this conductive extension.

changed_reading.before: We believed records acceptance of a proposition.
changed_reading.after: We believed claims settled allegiance whose hidden quality is meant to become legible through response to the delivered charge.

context_deltas.mechanism: The human testimony procedure can face concealment, competing claims, oath, and reversal; the focus request lodges the disciples' self-description directly with a witness not exposed to those failures.

activation_trace.role: The imperative asks for an attestation grounded in knowledge.
Formal testimony supplies the juridical frame into which the focus request is re-read.
Concealment names the failure against which a durable attestation must be guarded.
The oath image shows a human mechanism used to secure disputed testimony.
Truth fixed to reality supplies the criterion contested between testimonies.
Return or counter-return exposes testimony to procedural reversal.

structural_cues: 5:106-108 moves from testimony to concealment, replacement witnesses, stronger counter-testimony, and returned oaths.
The focus addresses the witness in the singular and places the predicate بأننا مسلمون inside the requested attestation.
Divine witness contrasts with the two-person and replacement-witness procedures.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies vulnerable human custody of testimony and the focus's direct appeal to God; I infer a claim deposited beyond concealment or counter-oath, while the live alternative is only an emphatic request to confirm present sincerity.

changed_reading.before: Bear witness intensifies the sincerity of the disciples' profession.
changed_reading.after: Bear witness registers their surrendered identity with the ultimate custodian against concealment, contest, and reversal.

context_deltas.mechanism: At the collective day the messengers are asked what response they received and defer unseen knowledge to God; the focus then supplies a particular recipients' answer and explicitly places it under God's witness.

activation_trace.role: The disciples' articulated reply provides the response-content sought by the preceding inquiry.
Their appeal identifies God as knower and attester of that reply.
A day or convocation that gathers people supplies the final-inquiry setting.
Returned speech or answer makes recipient response the explicit object of inquiry.
Hidden knowledge explains why the answer's final custody belongs to God.

structural_cues: 5:109 asks the gathered messengers ماذا أجبتم immediately before the sequence containing 5:111.
5:109's messengers answer لا علم لنا and name God as knower of unseen matters.
The focus's قالوا supplies a concrete response and واشهد directs its verification to that knower.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an inquiry about received answers followed by one recipients' answer and appeal to divine witness; I infer an answer preserved for final review, while the live alternative is that 5:111 only enumerates a past favor with no archival function.

changed_reading.before: The profession is dialogue inside a remembered past scene.
changed_reading.after: The profession is a recipient answer placed in divine custody for the inquiry into how messengers were answered.

context_deltas.mechanism: The repeated divine acts of strengthening, enabling speech, and teaching Jesus continue in the next وَإِذْ as concealed communication to his helpers, extending divine enablement from messenger to respondent body.

activation_trace.role: Divine inspiration makes the helpers' response another supplied enablement.
The helper image identifies a social body through which the messenger's mission can continue.
Strength conferred from outside supplies the enabling pattern before the focus.
Meaningful speech linking speakers supplies one enabled capacity in the preceding list.
Knowledge made manifest to the learner parallels knowledge quietly delivered to the helpers.

structural_cues: 5:110 repeatedly marks favors with إِذْ and first-person divine actions.
5:111 begins وَإِذْ and changes the recipient of divine action from Jesus to the helpers.
Speech and teaching in 5:110 are followed by hidden impartation and communal speech in 5:111.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a repeated temporal list of divine enablements and then revelation to the helpers; I infer that the helper community is an enabled extension of the mission, while the live alternative is that the final وَإِذْ introduces an independent favor without that transmission arrow.

changed_reading.before: God commands a pre-existing group and they choose to assent.
changed_reading.after: God's enablement propagates from messenger to helper body, whose assent and speech become a supplied continuation of the mission.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same disciples who say they believe are challenged as believers, request a descending meal, and explain that eating will settle their hearts, establish truth, and make them witnesses; profession is therefore an initial commitment that can precede embodied reassurance.

activation_trace.role: The doubled assent establishes the prior profession whose completeness the later request tests.
God is first asked to attest the disciples' state, establishing the initial witness direction.
The renewed believer label keeps the later request inside, rather than simply outside, the field of professed faith.
Capacity or ability makes divine capability the surface question that unsettles the profession.
Delivery downward converts hidden communication into a requested public and material arrival.
A food-bearing table gives the requested reassurance an inspectable and consumable body.
Settling and tranquility names the state still sought after the verbal profession.
The heart locates the unresolved settling inside the professing subjects.
Truthful speech supplies what the requested event is meant to verify.
The disciples seek to become attesters, reversing the focus request that God attest them.

structural_cues: 5:112 names the same disciples and again uses قال, directly after their 5:111 profession.
5:112 ends with إن كنتم مؤمنين despite the preceding آمنا.
5:113 gives an ordered purpose chain: eat, hearts settle, know truth, and become witnesses.
Witness direction changes from God witnessing the disciples in 5:111 to the disciples becoming witnesses in 5:113.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a prior profession, a renewed believer challenge, and the disciples' own reassurance sequence; I infer maturation through residual unsettledness rather than outright nullification, while the live alternative is that the request exposes a contradiction or is only a test of capability.

changed_reading.before: We believed declares complete and already stabilized certainty.
changed_reading.after: We believed is an initiating trust that can still seek embodied settling, verified truth, and a later role as witness.

context_deltas.mechanism: Jesus' witnessing is limited to his presence; after his life is taken, God alone guards and witnesses, and finally truthful people benefit from their truth. The focus appeal therefore places the disciples' claim in witness-custody that survives every human participant.

activation_trace.role: The direct appeal entrusts the profession to divine attestation at its outset.
Presence with observation distinguishes the bounded human witness from the unbounded divine one.
Taking the soul marks the temporal boundary after which human observation ceases.
Guarding and watchfulness supply God's continuing custody after that boundary.
Truthful speech identifies the enduring quality tested in the professed claim.
Benefit rather than harm supplies the final consequence of truth surviving scrutiny.

structural_cues: 5:116 interrogates Jesus about what he said to people.
5:117 contrasts كنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم with أنت الرقيب عليهم and أنت على كل شيء شهيد.
5:119 declares a day when the truthful benefit from their truth.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a temporal transfer from present human witness to divine watcher and a final benefit for truth; I infer that the focus appeal deliberately seeks witness beyond the scene, while the live alternative is a present-time prayer with no forward custody.

changed_reading.before: God is asked to confirm the disciples' current state.
changed_reading.after: Their self-description is entrusted to a witness who remains after messenger, speakers, and scene are gone and can test its truth at the final inquiry.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's form-distant ق ل ل target under focus ق و ل; it remains anchored at قَالُوا and yields a changed social mechanism, but downstream prose should call it a split-root branch image, not a lexical translation of the verb.

activation_trace.role: Carrying and rising with a load recasts the spoken response as taking up the weight of the confession.

changed_reading.before: They merely utter the expected answer.
changed_reading.after: Their saying images a community taking up and bearing the commitment it voices.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-material model is surprising because writing and evidentiary-mark branches are not the ordinary surface senses here; it remains anchored in أَوْحَيْتُ and وَٱشْهَدْ and explains their sequence, but downstream prose should render it as an 'as if inscribed' image rather than philological equivalence.

activation_trace.role: Writing or inscription makes the hidden communication act like a durable mark impressed into the group.
A sign that bears witness turns the resulting declaration into evidence of the prior communication.

changed_reading.before: Revelation and profession are transient turns in a conversation.
changed_reading.after: The hidden communication is as if inscribed into a community whose declaration becomes its evidentiary mark.

strongest_changes: The testimony procedure in 5:106-108 recasts وَٱشْهَدْ as durable registration against concealment and reversal.
The 5:112-113 request shows that ءَامَنَّا can precede embodied reassurance and reverses the witness direction from God witnessing them to them becoming witnesses.
The 5:117-119 transfer from Jesus' bounded presence to God's continuing watch makes the focus profession a truth-claim held beyond the lifetime of its human participants.
The final-response inquiry in 5:109 makes the disciples' قَالُوا read as an answer preserved before the knower of the unseen.
summary.what_was_special: The focus compresses hidden input, public answer, and surrendered identity into an appeal for divine evidentiary custody; the surrounding packet repeatedly toggles hidden and manifest states, answer and testimony, profession and reassurance, and human presence and enduring witness.
remaining_uncertainties: The table request may portray maturation within faith or expose a sharper contradiction in the prior profession.
The final inquiry may intentionally frame 5:111 as an archived answer, or the adjacency may only organize a list of favors.
The ق و ل to ق ل ل bearing image is packet-licensed but too form-distant to state without explicit containment.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Hidden imparting becomes public witness through purified helpers.** `و ح ي B001` is hidden imparting, `ح و ر B003` a purified helper, `ء م ن B002` trusting assent, and `ش ه د B002` testimony from knowledge. I infer a transmission arc from inward prompting to spoken belief and requested public attestation.
2. **Submission is a handing-over.** `س ل م B012` is handing over/letting go. The request “witness that we are submitting” reads as transfer of self-direction into acknowledged allegiance, not only a group name.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Hidden imparting is converted into open attestation.** Fixed **و ح ي / B001** (“hidden imparting of knowledge”) and **B004** (“Divine message and inspiration”) supply the inward arrival; the disciples answer with public belief and a demand for witness. 5:109 asked what response messengers received, while 5:112–5:113 will expose residual need for edible confirmation and settled hearts. I infer that inspiration seeks a social exterior in stated allegiance, even though the next request shows that declaration has not ended all unrest. The ayah reads as transfer from hidden address to witnessed commitment.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:112–5:113 exposed residual unrest after the witnessed declaration, confirming that open attestation can be genuine yet still seek bodily reassurance.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

source_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

tier_contracts.explicit_interest: Full source branch payload, except fields removed from all tiers.
tier_contracts.local_low_branch_safety: branch_ref, payload_tier, branch_image_ar, what_is_ar, status, branch_kind, and reviewed/dictionary concept/context gloss text.
tier_contracts.compact_rest: branch_ref, payload_tier, branch_image_ar, what_is_ar, status; a semantic fallback is added only when both Arabic fields are empty.

branch_policy.compact_gloss_policy: Reviewed gloss branches remain as branch_ref/payload_tier stubs; their branch records are trimmed, not filtered out.
branch_policy.note: Every root target and dictionary branch identity is retained. Branch payload detail is tiered from generation-time citations; non-full branches and reviewed gloss records are trimmed, not absent. Root lexicon and branch inventory availability never create interest.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
